thread:
rachel: Heads-up — ACME POC stuck. Demo call to /v1/generate returning 403 with 'tenant binding mismatch'. They hit this during the live walkthrough.
alex: Can you paste the exact curl and response body? Also which key are they using (trial vs enterprise)?
maria: If it's a tenant binding issue usually the org/project in header doesn't match the key's binding. Ask them to share the raw request (no secret in chat) or run `curl -v` and paste the response headers.
rachel: From the browser console they sent this (redacted):
Request:
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood-inference.example
Authorization: Bearer sk-poc_XXXXXXXX
X-Org-Id: acme-external
Content-Type: application/json
```

Response 403:
```
{"error":"forbidden","reason":"org_mismatch","expected_org":"acme","provided_org":"acme-external"}
```

alex: Hmm, looks like the key is bound to `acme` but they set `X-Org-Id: acme-external`. Two options: remove the extra header (let platform infer binding from key) or use the key that is bound to `acme-external`.
kevin: Also confirm they're not mixing a shadow/demo key with a tenant-scoped key. Shadow keys (shadow_) are unscoped for testing; svc_ or sk_ keys are tenant-bound depending on provisioning.
maria: Quick troubleshooting steps to give them: 
1) Run `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <THEIR_KEY>" https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/models` to see which tenant the key resolves to (response includes `x-tenant-id` header).
2) If they must send `X-Org-Id`, ensure it matches the `x-tenant-id` value.
3) Try removing `X-Org-Id` entirely and retry — our runtime will use the key binding by default.

alex: Example command to run (they can redact key):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-poc_XXXXX" https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

Look for headers in the response: `x-tenant-id`, `x-rate-limit-remaining`, and the full JSON error.
rachel: They replied — they were using the SDK sample that sets `org` from their env incorrectly (our docs/quickstart sets `REDWOOD_ORG` in some internal examples, they had `acme-external`). They didn't realize the portal key is already tenant-scoped.
kevin: Good find. Tell them to unset the env var or switch to the key that maps to `acme-external`. If they want, we can issue a temporary test key bound to the other tenant for the demo.
maria: If they prefer we can also do a quick key rotation: create a one-hour demo key scoped to `acme-external` and paste it into the shared demo sheet. I can provision that (dev tooling will log it in the ticket).
alex: Quick pricing note they asked — will rotating to a demo key affect billing? No — demo/test keys under our trial account are metered but not billed until they convert to a paid Dedicated contract. (High-level answer; redirect to billing for legal/contract questions.)
rachel: They ran the `curl -v` I suggested. Response headers show `x-tenant-id: acme` (so key indeed bound to `acme`). After removing the env-set `X-Org-Id` header, the generate call succeeded. Demo is green again. :tada:
deploy-bot: Incident note created: #POC-1952467890 — credential-binding-mismatch — resolved by clearing env header. Timestamp: 1952468130
rachel: Thanks all — will follow up with ACME to clean up their local env and update our quickstart to avoid this confusion. Adding a note for docs: call out tenant-bound keys vs explicit org headers. :memo:
